messages:
marta: Heads-up — after merging the v3 attention kernel path, we see a 12-18% p50 regression on 8k-seq perf for small batches. Not universal, mostly batch_size<=4 and seq_len in [3k..8k].

kai: Can you paste the perf numbers + runtime config snapshot? which model, dtype, quant?

marta: Test harness: gpt-like 7B, bf16, no extra quant, qkv_fuse=false. padding_ratio ~0.2. p50 baseline=42ms, post=48ms, p95 roughly same. Host mem pressure up ~300MB. Sequence distro attached.

alex: Do we still reuse the KV cache? v3 path allocates workspaces differently — could be extra memcpy for those small batches.

infra-bot: perf-ci: job #7841 finished. artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/perf/7841/metrics.json :white_check_mark:

marta: Quick allocator trace snippet: `workspace_alloc(threads=2, size=24MB) -> fallback to heap after fragmentation; memcpy 24MB * N` — small-batch workloads see fragmentation.

sam: @kai could the selector be misclassifying these as "mid/long" and forcing a larger workspace?

kai: Yep. Current heuristic: if padded_seq > 2048 -> v3. Our traffic: padded_seq ~3072 but active_seq (nonpad tokens) ~600-900 because of long cached prefixes. Kernel decision only looks at padded length.

marta: If we dispatch on an "active_seq" estimate rather than padded length, we avoid allocating v3-sized workspaces for many requests. Any correctness caveats?

alex: Seems reasonable, but ensure v3 kernel assumptions about memory layout still hold when active_seq < threshold. Also add telemetry: chosen_kernel, padded_seq, active_seq_est, workspace_bytes, memcpy_bytes per request to validate.

sam: Another quick mitigation: enable async memcpy for small batches to hide the copy cost. Try runtime flag `--attn_v3_prefer_async_memcpy=true`.

marta: I'll run a 24h perf sweep with (1) active_seq-driven dispatch, (2) async memcpy enabled. Will compare p50/p95 and memory footprint. If p50 improves >=8% without p95 regressions, plan to canary.

kai: If sweep passes, add a canary that applies a kernel_override for low-batch/high-padding routes. Also a rollback monitor: if p50 degrades >5% across canary nodes revert automatically.

marta: Attaching a short trace for reference:

```
REQ 0x7fb9: padded=3072 active=752 kernel=v3 workspace=28MB memcpy=24MB time=46.8ms
REQ 0x7fca: padded=3072 active=752 kernel=v2 workspace=6MB memcpy=2MB time=40.2ms
```

marta: :eyes: will post sweep results tomorrow.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary config pushed to cluster east-1-canary for route gpt7b:lowbatch-highpad

sam: Add a unit/integration test for the selector using synthetic prefix-cache states so this doesn't regress silently.

marta: Good call — adding test and telemetry. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
